activities.anchor: A health system is only as strong as this week
activities.caption: pair each blood component with its clock
activities.name: hsBloodMatch

config.prompt: The most perishable supply chain in medicine — pair each component with its shelf life:

pairs.right: refrigerated, around five to six weeks

config.why: The supply cannot be stockpiled or manufactured — it is continuously replaced, which is why a system is only as strong as its most recent collections.

config.prompt: Angioplasty works best fast, and systems organise themselves around the clock, not the hospital. Roughly what door-to-balloon time (minutes) do guidelines demand?
config.why: About 90 minutes — which is why London's 2000s redesign retrained ambulance crews to read the tracing in the field and drive straight to a 24/7 specialist hub.

activities.anchor: For time-critical conditions the opposite is often true
activities.caption: one line of the network note rewards proximity
activities.name: hsHubSpot

config.prompt: A note on emergency-network design — one line is wrong. Click it:
lines: Ambulance crews can be retrained to diagnose in the field and drive past the nearest department.
A few high-volume specialist centres, reached by bypass protocols, outperform a map dotted with low-volume general ones.
So the best network is the one that puts a small receiving unit in every town.
High-volume hospitals consistently lose fewer patients undergoing complex procedures.
Consolidation — eight receiving centres becoming fewer, busier ones — improved survival.
config.correction: The evidence supports consolidation: fewer, busier hubs reached by bypass protocols — proximity to a building is not proximity to competence.
config.why: The volume–outcome literature is the design principle: for time-critical care, concentrate the caseload.

activities.anchor: roughly 1.9 million neurons die each minute
activities.caption: place the marker on the thrombolysis window
activities.name: hsStrokePlace

config.prompt: Clot-dissolving drugs must arrive within a window measured from onset. Place the marker on that window (hours):
config.why: About 4.5 hours for clot-dissolving drugs; mechanical thrombectomy extends to 24 hours in selected patients whose imaging shows salvageable tissue — the DAWN trial stopped early.

activities.anchor: Immunisation policy is therefore the study of how trust, logistics and arithmetic interlock
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the population-level bargain
activities.name: hsHerdCloze

config.text: Immunisation creates individual memory; at scale, immune people block transmission, protecting even the %%0%% — herd immunity. Smallpox was declared eradicated in %%1%% because vaccination plus surveillance closed the gap everywhere.
config.hint: One blank names who the shield shelters; the other is the year the declaration was made.

activities.anchor: a platform built for exactly this, while authorisation still awaited
activities.caption: rebuild the 63-day sequence
activities.name: hsCovidOrder

config.prompt: The fastest pipeline on record — drag the sequence into order:
items: The viral genome is published (11 January 2020)
Vaccine design begins on the published sequence
The first dose enters a trial — 63 days after the sequence
Manufacturing scales at financial risk before approval
Authorisation waits for full-scale trials with tens of thousands of volunteers
config.why: The compression was in paperwork queues and parallel production, not in the evidence — and the stockpiles that matter are bought in peacetime or not at all.

activities.anchor: pay the difference in emergency departments
activities.caption: walk the primary-care budget decision
activities.name: hsPrimaryBranch

config.root: Two system designs, one budget. Walk the trade.

start.text: The ministry can fund a strong first-contact layer or let hospitals absorb everything. Which design?

choices.label: Fund strong primary care — gatekeeping, continuity, prevention
choices.feedback: Most illness is minor, chronic or preventable — handled where it is cheapest.

choices.label: Skip it; emergency departments will catch what comes
choices.feedback: The costliest door in medicine becomes the safety net.

primary.text: The cross-national evidence: better outcomes at lower total cost than specialist-heavy systems — hospitals reserved for what hospitals are for.

ed.text: The bill lands downstream: unserved first-contact care arrives at the emergency door, and the system pays hospital prices for problems a clinic would have cleared.

config.why: Primary care is the system's highest-leverage layer — the mechanism is arithmetic as much as medicine.

activities.caption: which curve is the training lag?
activities.name: hsWorkforceTrace

config.prompt: A training pipeline is funded today. Which curve shows workforce supply over the following years?
config.why: The supply curve answers the funding decision years late — which is why today's shortages were decided long ago, why migration fills the gap, and why the WHO adopted a voluntary code on ethical recruitment (2010).
